title: Recurrent networks classify cancer-bearing mouse ovary images
summary: A convolutional LSTM classified optical-coherence tomography of excised ovaries from sixteen mice, half from an ovarian-cancer model and half wild-type controls. Tissue pathology supported the disease labels. Across repeated leave-one-animal-out evaluations, mean AUC was 0.81; the best run reached 0.98. This is a small retrospective preclinical imaging validation, not human ovarian-cancer screening or evidence of earlier detection or improved treatment outcomes.
ai_technology: Convolutional long short-term memory; VGG and three-dimensional CNN comparisons

source_review.scope: Primary relevant animal-cohort/reference, preprocessing, learned architecture, animal-wise validation Methods, Results/Table2 and limitations; cited earlier experimental protocols not independently re-reviewed. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Existing ex-vivo ovarian OCT recordings from eight cancer-model and eight wild-type mice, with pathological verification and leave-one-animal-out testing repeated ten times. Mean convolutional-LSTM AUC .81 is distinguished from the selected peak .98.
evidence.unknown: Human diagnostic transfer, clinical screening, early-stage detection and benefit remain unestablished. Only sixteen animals and one held-out animal per fold limit uncertainty estimates; peak-run performance is not representative average performance.
evidence.ai_role: The convolutional LSTM learns sequential relationships between depth-resolved OCT slices and classifies tissue from cancer-model versus wild-type animals, using pathology-supported labels.
